known_facts_book1: The Wicked Witch of the East, who had held the Munchkins in bondage for many years before the story opens.
Is killed offstage at the very start when Dorothy's cyclone-borne house falls on her; she is found already dead, only her feet sticking out from under the house.
Her body dries up and vanishes in the sun, leaving nothing but the Silver Shoes she was proud of.
Enchanted the Tin Woodman's axe long ago, at the bribe of a lazy old woman, to stop him marrying a Munchkin girl.
Never appears alive, never speaks, and meets no one on the page.

known_relations_book1.Dorothy: The girl whose falling house kills her; they never meet or speak.
known_relations_book1.Munchkins: The people she held enslaved until her death freed them.
known_relations_book1.Tin Woodman: Whose axe she enchanted, costing him his flesh body.

known_facts_book1: A beautiful princess and sorceress of long ago, known only from the legend the King of the Winged Monkeys tells.
Lived in a ruby palace and was betrothed to the handsome young man Quelala.
When the Winged Monkeys dropped Quelala into a river in mischief, she nearly had them drowned, then instead bound them to serve the owner of the Golden Cap three times.
Never appears in the present action of the book; she exists only in the past-tense legend, never speaking to Dorothy or the travellers.

known_relations_book1.Quelala: Her betrothed, whose mistreatment by the Monkeys she punished.
known_relations_book1.Winged Monkeys: Whom she bound to the Golden Cap as punishment.
known_relations_book1.King of the Winged Monkeys: Whose grandfather's band she punished, and who tells her story.

known_facts_book1: A handsome and good young man of long ago, betrothed to the princess Gayelette, known only from the Winged Monkey King's legend.
Was seized in fun by the Winged Monkeys and dropped into a river, ruining his fine silks and velvet.
Being the Golden Cap's first owner, spoke a kind word for the Monkeys so that Gayelette spared them, on the terms of the three-command binding.
Never appears in the present action of the book and never meets Dorothy or the travellers.
